meta.title: Reading log
meta.subtitle: Round 1 of 2
meta.headline: Before you build anything — what is this for?
meta.lede: You bounced off Goodreads twice, which tells me more about what you **don't** want than what you do. Five questions to pin down the job and what you want handed back. The next round gets specific.
meta.closingAsk: Update the scope from these answers, then tell me what is still open.

scope.label: What we're trying to achieve
scope.text: Not agreed yet. Something between a private record and a habit you actually keep up.

scope.label: What we hand over
scope.text: Not agreed yet. You can write code, so this could be a plan, a first cut, or a quick trial.

scope.label: What's in and what's out
scope.text: Assumed for now: you are the only person who ever sees this. Nothing social, nothing shared.
scope.assumption: You bounced off Goodreads over the social side twice, so I am treating that as out until told otherwise.

scope.label: How we know it's done
scope.text: Assumed for now: it works if you log three books in a row without going back to a notes app.
scope.assumption: Sticking with it is the only outcome that matters here, so I am assuming that is the test.

scope.label: Fixed facts we work inside
scope.text: It has to work on the train home, on a phone, and logging a book must beat six taps.
scope.assumption: Both come straight from your message; I am treating them as fixed rather than as preferences.

constraints.label: Phone:
constraints.text: this happens on the train, not at a desk

constraints: Faster than six taps, or it has already failed
No account, no feed, no friends

context.title: What I took from your message
context.note: Two failed attempts at Goodreads is the most useful thing you told me. It rules out a whole shape of product, which is why none of the questions below ask about sharing.

items.desc: where you finish books, and where signal comes and goes
the bar Goodreads failed to clear, so it is the one to beat

questions.context: You said you want to track books, but tracking is not a goal on its own. What you want to be able to do later decides almost everything else.
breakdown: A record to look back on: what matters is that nothing is ever lost.
A habit to keep up: what matters is that logging is so quick you never skip it.
questions.question: What is the log actually for?
questions.why: You have bounced off two apps already, so the thing that has been failing is the habit, not the storage.
questions.switchIf: Pick the record if you have years of reading elsewhere that you want to bring in and keep.

options.label: A permanent record
options.detail: Complete and lasting; slower to add to.

options.label: A habit you keep
options.detail: Fast enough that you never skip a book.

options.label: Something to share
options.detail: Ruled out by both Goodreads attempts.

questions.context: Goodreads took six taps partly because it asked for a lot. What you capture per book is the difference between two seconds and thirty.
breakdown: Title alone: almost instant, and you will fill in the rest never.
A few fields: still quick, and enough to be worth re-reading later.
questions.question: What do you want to capture per book?
questions.why: Title plus a date plus one line of what you thought is the most you can type on a train and still do it every time.
questions.switchIf: Go with title alone if you know you will resent typing anything at all on a phone.

options.label: Just the title
options.detail: One field, nothing to think about.

options.label: Title, date, one line
options.detail: Enough to enjoy re-reading in a year.

options.label: Full details and a rating
options.detail: This is roughly what you already quit twice.

questions.context: The train is the hard part. Underground stretches and bad signal are exactly when you have just finished something and want to log it.
breakdown: Works with no signal: you can log anywhere and it catches up later.
Needs signal: less to build, and dead on the part of the journey that matters.
questions.example: The app saves to the phone the moment you tap save, and quietly copies it up whenever a connection comes back.
questions.question: Should it work with no signal?
questions.why: The one moment this has to work is the moment you are least likely to have a connection, and the extra work is small.
questions.switchIf: Skip it if your commute has signal the whole way and you would rather have something working sooner.

options.label: Works with no signal
options.detail: Log anything, anywhere; it catches up later.

options.label: Needs a connection
options.detail: Simpler to build, useless in a tunnel.

questions.context: You can write code, so what you need from me is not necessarily code. The three answers below take very different amounts of your evenings.
breakdown: A plan: you build it at your own pace, with the decisions already made.
A first working cut: faster to something real, less room to change your mind.
questions.question: What should I hand you at the end?
questions.why: You said you have not decided what to build, which is a thinking problem rather than a typing one, and you can clearly do the typing.
questions.switchIf: Ask for the working cut if you would rather have something on your phone this week than understood.

options.label: A short build plan
options.detail: Decisions made, ordered steps, nothing more.

options.label: A first working cut
options.detail: Something you can log a book into this week.

options.label: A quick trial first
options.detail: One rough version to test the habit, then decide.

questions.context: Whatever I hand back can carry extras. Choosing now stops me guessing and stops the plan sprawling into things you would skip.
breakdown: The data shape: worth it if you might move the log somewhere else one day.
A screen sketch: worth it if the six-taps problem is really a layout problem.
questions.question: Which of these would you actually use?
questions.why: The tap count is a screen-design problem more than a storage one, so the sketch earns its place and the rest can wait.
questions.switchIf: Add the data shape too if you suspect you will want this on a laptop eventually.

options.label: A sketch of the logging screen
options.detail: Where every tap goes, and why.

options.label: The shape of the saved data
options.detail: So the log outlives whatever you build.

options.label: A way in from Goodreads
options.detail: Only useful if you want the old data.
